text:
git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(exceptions): the uncaught report printed the WRAPPER and dropped what it wrapped

`throw new X($msg, 0, $previous)` is how a library says what it was doing when
something underneath it failed, and php prints every link of that chain: the
deepest one under `Fatal error: Uncaught`, each later one under `Next`, and the
`  thrown in ...` tail once, for the exception actually thrown.

elephc printed the OUTERMOST link and stopped. MEASURED on `php -n` 8.5.6:

    $a = new RuntimeException("first");
    $b = new LogicException("second", 0, $a);
    throw new TypeError("third", 0, $b);

    php    : RuntimeException: first  → Next LogicException → Next TypeError
    elephc : TypeError: third

The half that says what went WRONG is the half that was thrown away. A wrapper's
own message is almost always the vague one — "an exception occurred while
executing the query" — and the report named only that.

`__rt_report_uncaught_exception` now walks to the deepest `previous`, reports it,
and climbs back link by link, finding each parent by walking down from the head
again: the chain is a handful of links and the report runs once, at exit. Every
link gets its own `Stack trace:` block, and the tail line is suppressed for all
but the last by passing the writer a zero line — the same "no origin, print
nothing" rule it already applied.

Two tests here asserted FULL equality against output that predates the stack-trace
block: they expected no `Stack trace:` at all, and one expected a
`DivisionByZeroError` with no location. Both had been failing before this change —
verified by rebuilding with HEAD's reporter — and both described an engine that no
longer exists. Their expectations are now the measured `php -n` 8.5.6 bytes for
the same programs, which is what elephc already printed. One is renamed:
`synthesized_error_omits_the_location_and_still_exits_255` no longer omits it.

Verified: 8 uncaught-report tests, 125 exception tests, 1532 unit tests, and the
183-program round-8 corpus unchanged at 180 identical. x86_64 assembles clean; the
CI x86 shard remains its only execution oracle.
